lorecomics.title: Comics and lore
lorecomics.intro: With the introduction of public rooms, jiggie has started seeing regulars join and chat to each other. The chat is mostly filled with autism but some lore does develop ocassionally. One autist (ToJ: The One Jigger) decided to use his actually impressive artistic talent to turn the chat lore into high quality comics. He's also responsible for the pixel art animations and other art assets you see around the site.

rules.title: Rules - Jiggie
rules.uploadIntro: You are allowed to upload anything to be used as an image/video for a puzzle except the following:
rules.category1: (Cat. 1) CSAM, as defined by Article 2.3 of
rules.law: the relevant Act in Japanese Law
rules.category1Note: Note that Jiggie is cooperating with NCMEC and infractions will result in reports to authorities, and failure to report infringing content may result in you being considered recipient of such content.
rules.category2: (Cat. 2) Things a local authority asks me to remove (DMCA and so on...).
rules.reportIntro: When reporting, you will be asked to quote an infraction code as a proof that you have actually read the rules. You can click the boxes for easy copy.
rules.reportCases: The report function should be used in one of the following cases:
rules.roomContains: The room contains multimedia content of:
rules.cat2: Category 2 (Copyright infringement) is handled exclusively through
rules.vpn: You, as the Host of a room, suspect a user is evading bans using VPNs/Proxies. In which case, you should report the room after banning a couple times to collect enough IPs (
rules.scripts: You suspect a user is using automated scripts to grief (
rules.ban3: You want to get a 3-day long site-wide ban (
rules.reportNot: The report function should NOT be used in the following cases:
rules.mean: Someone is being mean to you in the chat
rules.dislikeUser: Someone you don't like is in the chat
rules.dislikeMusic: Someone is putting music you personally dislike in the jukebox
rules.dislikePuzzle: Someone is using content you personally dislike as a puzzle
rules.grief: Someone is griefing the room (That's the host responsibility, my responsibility is limited to giving them tools to deal with griefing)
rules.dataIntro: Personal, potentially identifying data may be collected, and may be purged only under certain circumstances. Collected means the information remains saved on our server.
rules.mediaPurge: Images and Videos, purged either on low disk space, or after one minute of no activity if the self-destruct option was used.
rules.jukebox: Jukebox songs are cached locally, purged on low disk space
rules.ipRoom: Collected and associated to a created room. Preserved until the room is deleted, either through the self-destruct option, or manually through the /del chat command
rules.ipReport: Collected when reporting a room. Deleted when the report is handled, unless it results in the creation of a ban or warning.
rules.ipAntiAbuse: Collected for certain anti-abuse measures, like vote kicking, jukebox, scores, room-specific banlists (purged when the room is deleted), global ban lists (purged never), warning (purged when the warning is acknowledged).
rules.ipLog: Collected through the webserver access log, associates the IP with any resource served over HTTP, purged on low disk-space (it's on a different disk than the multimedia content so the purge is much less frequent).
rules.nicknameCollected: Collected when chatting, lifetime is tied to the room's.
rules.messagesCollected: Collected when you send a message in chat, lifetime is tied to the room's.
rules.harsh: You can't read basic instructions and don't know how to delete a puzzle you've created, and you're solliciting me to clean your ass up, fuck you. Either stop thinking people actually give a fuck about the faceless fatass public toilet you call a girlfriend or stop plastering her everywhere.
rules.thirdPartyText: Your IP address may be collected by external services when using the search function on the Jukebox to search for videos to use as songs.

modals.muteIpDescription: Mute based on the player's IP address. This method is more specific and targetable than ASN.
modals.muteAsnDescription: Mute based on ASN (Autonomous System Number, typically an ISP or large organization). Use this as a last resort, for example, if you suspect a user is frequently changing IPs within the same VPN service or ISP.
modals.exactIpDescription: Matches only the specific IP address. This has no risk of false positives but is the easiest to evade if the user has a dynamic IP.
modals.narrowSubnetDescription: Matches a small subnetwork (e.g., /28 or /29) containing the target IP. Low risk of affecting innocent users, slightly harder to evade.
modals.largeSubnetDescription: Matches a larger subnetwork (e.g., /24) containing the target IP. Higher risk of false positives, but significantly harder to evade.

help.title: Help
help.invite: Invite others by sending them the link from the address bar.
help.cog: Use cog icon next to your user name to change your user settings.
help.d1: Hold <kbd class="kbd">Ctrl</kbd> key to lock or unlock pieces in place.
help.d2: Use <kbd class="kbd">Left Mouse Click</kbd> and <kbd class="kbd">Right Mouse Click</kbd> to rotate pieces left and right (only if rotation is enabled), you can also use <kbd class="kbd">F</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">G</kbd> or <kbd class="kbd">Arrow Keys</kbd> to rotate the pieces that you selected or picked up.
help.d3: Use <kbd class="kbd">Ctrl + Z</kbd> to undo last move.
help.d4: Use <kbd class="kbd">Home</kbd> to jump to initial view location and zoom.
help.d5: Use <kbd class="kbd">End</kbd> to view all pieces.
help.d6: Use <kbd class="kbd">Delete</kbd> to clear chat log.
help.d7: Use <kbd class="kbd">Q</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">W</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">E</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">A</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">S</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">D</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">Z</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">X</kbd>, <kbd class="kbd">C</kbd> keys to jump to one of 9 sections of the board (from top left to bottom right).
help.d8: <kbd class="kbd">Double Click</kbd> a piece, selected by an inactive player, to free it up.
help.m1: Move the board by dragging from empty space.
help.m2: Use another <kbd class="kbd">Finger</kbd> to move around while holding a piece.
help.m3: Use <kbd class="kbd">Two Fingers</kbd> to pinch zoom.
help.m4: Start rectangle selection by double tapping empty space to select multiple pieces.
help.m5: Double tap to release selected pieces.
help.m6: Click <kbd class="kbd">Chat Button</kbd> in bottom right corner to chat.
help.chatHelp: /help: shows the chat commands with usage and description

tour.camera1: Use <kbd class="kbd">Right Mouse Button</kbd> or <kbd class="kbd">Middle Mouse Button</kbd> to move around the board (use middle mouse button on Opera or disable gestures).
tour.camera2: Pinch to zoom, scroll or use <kbd class="kbd">+</kbd>/<kbd class="kbd">-</kbd>
tour.controls1: Use <kbd class="kbd">Left Mouse Button</kbd> to drag the pieces.
tour.selection1: Hold <kbd class="kbd">Shift</kbd> key to select multiple pieces.
tour.selection2: Use <kbd class="kbd">Left Mouse Button</kbd> on empty space and drag selection rectangle to select multiple pieces.
tour.spread1: Hold <kbd class="kbd">Space</kbd> to do a spread alignment on the selected pieces.
tour.spread2: With <kbd class="kbd">Shift</kbd>+<kbd class="kbd">Space</kbd> you can gather the pieces together.
tour.spread3: And with <kbd class="kbd">Alt</kbd>+<kbd class="kbd">Space</kbd> you can spread them apart.
tour.usersListText: There you can see the list of users in the room (including yourself).
tour.chatInput1: Press <kbd class="kbd">Enter</kbd> to chat, then type your message and press <kbd class="kbd">Enter</kbd> to send it.
tour.chatInput2: To see special commands type <kbd class="kbd">/help</kbd>
tour.roomMenuText: For more options and extra help you can click on the room menu button.
